mechanism: Static vector TA functions (SMA/EMA/BB/StdDev/MACD/RSI/Stoch/ATR/Momentum/AO/AC) accept any vector, not just PRICE_* constants, so derived series such as high−low or multi-column OHLC SMA/momentum matrices become immediate sensor features without iCustom handles.
data_needed: OHLC (or any derived numeric series) as MQL5 vectors; chosen period/shift; optional matrix stacking of multiple transforms
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 demo scripts; generic Symbol()/Period() plotting
why_new_for_mis: MIS usually wires fixed built-in buffers; this treats any engineered series as a first-class indicator input for parallel feature collection into ML matrices.
quote: wouldn't it be awesome if we can pass different inputs and parameters to the indicators for the sake of observing new patterns in the market?

mechanism: Discrete Rademacher (±1 square waves, period 2^N) and Walsh (sine/cosine-like) coefficient banks project a price window into orthogonal weights: order-0 ≈ SMA; higher Rademacher orders act as average speeds of nested linear trends; Walsh sine parts track trends while cosine parts mark trend-change moments (Hartley and even-cosine Rademacher variants add asymmetric trend vs center-referenced smoothing).
data_needed: Close (or chosen price) window of length 2^N; max function order P; optional line-mode last-value or order≥1 oscillator (zeroed order-0)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MT5 charts; no single pair locked; EA tests on price vs indicator / dual-line / oscillator levels
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a binary orthogonal multi-scale trend vs change decomposition without FFT, with explicit cosine/Hartley channels aimed at regime-change timing.
quote: Sine functions track trends, while cosine functions track moments of trend changes.

mechanism: Triangular window coefficients (and integer sub-period harmonics) build a centered multi-wave smoother that highlights wave-like cycles; sawtooth (asymmetric LWMA-like multi-tooth) coefficients interpret motion as trend and stack waves into nested trend channels—even wave counts average the trend, odd counts pin it; time-separated independent waves and a mean-stripped Wave Osc sum wave weights only.
data_needed: Price series; iPeriod (≥3 triangle / ≥2 sawtooth); NumWave; wave type; optional shift
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MT5; strategy EAs on price/indicator cross and oscillator extrema
why_new_for_mis: Asymmetric sawtooth multi-tooth channel tightness is a concrete regime-strength sensor distinct from SMA/EMA envelopes.
quote: One could say that the indicator constructs trend channels. And the closer the channel lines are to each other, the more pronounced the trend is.

mechanism: Partition the AnalysisPeriod high–low range into tick-sized PriceLevel bins; accumulate bar-touch time_spent per bin (optimized O(n×k)); normalize to presence_percent in [1%,100%] and color-map red→blue. Blue/high presence = magnetic high-activity liquidity; red/low = fast-passage / time-gap zones. Sliding MaxHistory window keeps the map current.
data_needed: OHLC bars; AnalysisPeriod; MaxHistory; TickSize (0=auto); transparency; instrument Point
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex (AnalysisPeriod 300–500, MaxHistory 5000–8000); stocks (200–300 / 3000–5000); any MT5 symbol
why_new_for_mis: Liquidity sensed as dwell-time density on price, not volume profile alone—pairs with time-gap anomalies as a dual map of where price lingers vs rushes.
quote: The longer the time, the "hotter" the zone, the more important it is for the market.

mechanism: Build custom-symbol rates B₃D=(P,V,T,σ) from source M15: typical price, returns, price acceleration, volume change rate, and LookbackPeriod rolling stdev of returns; ScaleValue min-max maps metrics into ScaleMin–ScaleMax (3–9) and writes synthetic OHLC so chart/EA pipelines consume multi-dimensional market state as a tradable symbol.
data_needed: Source symbol M15 OHLC+tick_volume; LookbackPeriod; HistoryDays; MinSpreadMultiplier; VolumeBrick; ScaleMin/Max
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD→EURUSD_3D example; M15 base; notes for H1/D1 and low-liquidity longer TFs
why_new_for_mis: Encodes price, volume intensity, cyclic time, and local volatility into one synthetic feed MIS can subscribe to like any symbol.
quote: 3D bars combine four key dimensions in a single chart: price … volume … time … volatility

mechanism: ClassifyMarketState maps (price_change, volatility, volume_ratio) into {strong bull, weak bull, neutral, weak bear, strong bear} with volatility- and volume-scaled strong/weak thresholds; EnhancedMarkovChain learns transition frequencies; paired with 256-dim SSM (state=A·state+B·input) for long quantitative memory beyond first-order Markov.
data_needed: OHLC+volume features (~400 incl. RSI/stoch/ATR/autocorr/session); H1 training windows; ALGLIB Markov matrices
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 training; M15 live test Jun–Jul 2025; synthetic 3D-bar feature symbol
why_new_for_mis: Explicit five-regime discrete state machine with adaptive thresholds plus SSM continuous memory is a ready MIS regime+change stack, not a black-box class label alone.
quote: The system classifies the current market state as one of five: strong rise, weak rise, flat, weak fall, or strong fall.

mechanism: Context analyzer blends short/medium/long/episodic memories with weights that rise for short-term when input_volatility is high and shift to longer horizons when calm (plus episodic weight on input_complexity); quantum resonance/interference/decoherence modulate features before transformer attention and class-weighted Gaussian-ish targets.
data_needed: Same 400-feature matrix; running volatility and complexity scalars; Adam/backprop through quantum layers
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1/M15; 3D bars custom symbol features
why_new_for_mis: Makes the neural sensor’s memory horizon itself a volatility-conditioned regime dial—useful as an MIS meta-sensor of which history depth currently matters.
quote: When the market becomes volatile, the system relies more on short-term memory … During calm periods, on the contrary, long-term memory is activated

mechanism: FracDiff = |recent high fractal − low fractal|; uptrend oscillator = distance from candle body extreme to PSAR / FracDiff; downtrend analog with opposite body side. Unitless cross-asset histogram; FracDiff≫PSAR gap → muted (high vol, weak momentum); FracDiff≪gap → spikes; zero cross marks PSAR flip.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Gold, GBPJPY called out as cross-comparable; MT4/MT5 any TF
why_new_for_mis: Single candle-local, instrument-normalized sensor jointly reading trend (PSAR) and swing volatility (fractal range) without separate panels.
quote: normalize the gap between price and the Parabolic SAR by the price range defined by recent fractal points.

mechanism: Replace fractal range with ATR(period): uptrend hist=(high−SAR)/ATR, downtrend=(low−SAR)/ATR (ATR≠0). ATR averaging damps single-bar spike noise of V1; ATR>PSAR gap shrinks hist, ATR<gap expands it; typical band ±5, extremes near ±7.
data_needed: OHLC; iSAR(pstep,pMax); iATR(AtrPeriod default 7); dual up/down buffers
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Cross-market normalized (e.g. XAUUSD vs GBPJPY); H4 USDJPY threshold example (±2.5)
why_new_for_mis: Volatility-context PSAR distance is a cleaner regime/momentum/divergence sensor than raw PSAR or spike-prone fractal normalization.
quote: the ATR provides a smoothed, continuous reading of the average trading range … inherently filters out the noise of anomalous price spikes

mechanism: One-hidden-layer MLPRegressor outputs (μ, σ²) of next price increment with linear μ and Softplus σ²; trains under GaussianNLLLoss (weighted MSE + ½log σ²) via ALGLIB L-BFGS so predicted variance tracks feature-dependent heteroscedasticity; indicator plots mean plus confidence bands.
data_needed: Close increments over InpPeriodWindow as features; InpSamples training rows; InpShift test bars; hidden width; epochs
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD shown for mean+95% CI; Forex increments generally
why_new_for_mis: MIS gets a full conditional distribution sensor (expected move and uncertainty) instead of point forecasts or constant-vol residuals.
quote: our model provides the trader with not just a point forecast, but the full conditional distribution of the target variable.

mechanism: EA draws higher-TF vertical separators, optional bull/bear body fills, open/close horizontals, and nested minor-TF verticals onto the active lower-TF chart (objects OBJPROP_BACK), refreshing on HTF/minor new bars so intra-bar structure of HTF candles is a live multi-scale structure map.
data_needed: Major TF OHLC lookback; optional Minor1/Minor2 TFs; colors/widths; refresh seconds
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Examples H1 major with M1 chart context; M30/M15 minors; M1–MN selectable
why_new_for_mis: Treats HTF candle anatomy (body fill, wick open/close, nested minors) as an explicit multi-scale structure sensor stream, not just chart chrome.
quote: observing the real-time body fill effect of higher-timeframe candles forming directly on the lower-timeframe chart

mechanism: Time-independent Kagi: extend vertical only on meaningful close moves; reverse after fixed price-step or % reversal; track shoulders/waists; Yang (thick) when breaking prior shoulder (demand), Yin (thin) when breaking prior waist (supply). Thin→thick and thick→thin flips are classic regime-change signals; non-repainting OBJ_TREND construction on closed bars.
data_needed: Close+time of kagiTimeframe; reversalType (percent|step) and reversalValue; Yin/Yang colors; lookBackBars
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: JPN225 live demo with kagitrader.set; default PERIOD_M10 example; any symbol/TF
why_new_for_mis: Supply/demand regime encoded as line thickness flips independent of clock time—useful noise-robust change sensor alongside candle TFs.
quote: Thin => Thick = Buy signal. Thick => Thin = Sell signal.

mechanism: Map each price level to an integer (round or ×PriceMultiplier); count primes in PrimeSearchRadius via Eratosthenes cache; convert counts to density percent and paint red(low)–blue(high) rectangles over AnalysisPeriod. Blue zones hypothesized as mathematically dense ‘anchors’ coinciding with reversals; used to rank S/R strength and filter false breakouts.
data_needed: OHLC range; AnalysisPeriod; MaxHistory; PriceMultiplier or UseIntegerPrices; PrimeSearchRadius; color/transparency
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Five major FX pairs, three cryptos, two commodities; H1–D1 test window ~5 months; EURUSD 1.0850×10000 example
why_new_for_mis: Level-importance prior from number-theoretic density around price integers—orthogonal to volume/time heat maps already common in MIS.
quote: Blue zones (areas of high prime-number density) coincide with trend reversal points in 55–58% of cases.
